name: Kentucky
sources: Flat rate 3.5% for tax years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2026: 2025 HB 1 (Acts Ch. 1), KRS 141.020 (apps.legislature.ky.gov/record/25RS/HB1.html)
2026 standard deduction $3,360: Kentucky DOR news release, Sept 4, 2025 (revenue.ky.gov/News/Pages/Kentucky-DOR-Announces-2026-Standard-Deduction.aspx)

Itemized deductions limited to mortgage interest, charitable gifts and a few miscellaneous items, allowed whether or not you itemize federally: 2025 Kentucky Schedule A (revenue.ky.gov/Forms/740-NP Schedule A (2025).pdf); 2025 Form 740
$40 personal tax credit for each person 65+: Kentucky Schedule ITC, Section B (revenue.ky.gov/Forms/Schedule ITC 2023.pdf)
provisional: The $40 credit for each person 65 or older is from the 2023 Schedule ITC (fixed in statute, KRS 141.020)
notes: Local occupational license taxes on wages and self-employment income (commonly 1–2.5% in cities and counties) are not included.
Married couples who both have income can file separately on a combined return and each take the $3,360 standard deduction; this estimate uses one.
